newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai property aid agency has 10 bln baht capital.
newsitem.headline: Thai property aid agency has 10 bln baht capital.

text.p: Thailand's Property Loan Management Organisation (PLMO) initially will have 10 billion baht available when it begins refinancing projects later this month, a senior central bank official said on Wednesday.
The PLMO is aiming to alleviate the debt burdens of troubled Thai financiers and developers by refinancing selected real estate schemes in the ailing local property market.

"We expect the first deal to be signed within the next two weeks... we can't say the exact value right now but the value is up to 10 billion, something like that. We have to have up to 10 billion baht prepared," a senior central bank official told Reuters.
Financial institutions have until June 15 to submit applications to join the PLMO's aid scheme, the official said.

"The PLMO has sent a letter to all financial institutions involved telling them that the PLMO is now in operation and that it is able to receive applications to join. The deadline for joining is June 15," he said.
The government is attempting to support the troubled Thai property market with the PLMO's scheme as the sector has been hit by oversupply and slowing economic growth.

Initial interest in the program from local financial institutions is considerable with some applications already received, a further 10-15 imminent, and several more expected before the deadline, the official said.

"A lot of financial institutions have called us. We only recently sent the letter so a lot say they need some more time to study the program and get a decision from their board ... but we expect them to do that before June 15," he said.

Private forecasters believe around 300,000 residential units currently stand empty in Bangkok's troubled property market. By supporting the market, the authorities are attemptimg to protect the financial system which has around 8OO billion baht ($33 billion) in credit tied up in the depressed real estate sector.
High interest rates and slack demand have forced property firms into liquidity crunches.

Independent valuations on properties to be considered for assistance must be conducted by firms listed among 15 local valuers approved by the central bank and the Securities Exchange Commission, the official said.
